The skill and eval edits hold and the card is delivered. One published docs row this round makes false is owed, one line.

**Gates on this head:** `l1-face --pr 35877` CLEAN (13 items, none flagged). Check-runs at d4661ccc: 32 success, 15 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending. `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` both success. Dogfood battery not owed.

**C1. `content/docs/getting-started/build-with-claude-code.mdx:419` still sends a business question to `objectstack-query`.**
- The row reads: "Queries & reports over records | `objectstack-query` | "Show me the count of open tickets per priority, using an aggregation."". The page introduces the table as "each row is a real prompt you can give verbatim", with "Skill the agent loads" as the column.
- After this PR, query's description says: "Not for a business question answered from the app's records: a number, ranking or governed metric (objectstack-ask)". "Show me the count of open tickets per priority" is exactly that shape: a count broken down by a field, asked for as an answer, not as code. It is the near twin of ask's positive case 4 ("list the ten customers with the most open tickets right now"). The PR's own rewrite of query case 3 draws the line at writing an aggregation in code ("In our ObjectStack app's server code, write one ObjectQL aggregation …"). The docs prompt is on the other side of that line.
- So the round makes this published row false, or at best leaves it contested. Per the L1 rule, a published defect the round makes false is fixed in the same PR.
- **Fix:** reword the prompt so it asks for code, matching the new query case 3. For example: "In a hook, write the ObjectQL aggregation that counts open tickets per priority." The row's "Queries & reports over records" label can stay, or become "Queries in app code". It is one cell in a hand-written page outside any generated block.

**What I checked (holds):**
- **The card is delivered.** All three Asks and Done-when items are met:
  - Query's description drops "or shaping a records query or aggregation sent over MCP". Its "Not for" now names `objectstack-ask` first, for "a business question answered from the app's records: a number, ranking or governed metric".
  - Query case 3 is reworded into server-code aggregation and stays `should_trigger: true`. That keeps the bundle's only aggregation positive, which the card allows ("or reword it to shaping a query in code").
  - The changeset is `'@objectstack/skills': patch` (`packages/skills` is the package).
  - `Fixes` is right.
- **The two descriptions now agree.** Ask says: "Do not use … for writing a query in application code (see objectstack-query)". Query says: Not for the business question (objectstack-ask). `skills/objectstack-query/rules/aggregation.md:5` already said: "Answering a user's question over MCP (`aggregate_records`) … see objectstack-ask". Query's own SKILL.md body has no other MCP claim (`git grep -i MCP` over `skills/objectstack-query/`, evals aside: that one line).
- **The evals.**
  - The new query case 3 does not collide with ask's negative case 5. Both are ObjectQL aggregations in server code, a positive for query and a negative for ask.
  - Ask's new negative case 7 (add a picklist field to `account` over MCP) is ask's own "Do not use for building or changing metadata" clause. That is N3 of contract review 7040518746.
  - Both files are valid JSON with unique ids.
- **The mirror.** `content/docs/ai/skills-reference.mdx` changes only the query description paragraph, word for word as the SKILL.md frontmatter. CI's skill-docs sync is green.
- **Size.** `check-skills-token-ratchet` on this head: query 4607/5547, ask 1875/1877 (unchanged, only its evals moved), so no ceiling was raised.
- **The area call on description length.** Query's description is now 477 characters. No gate reads description length: I found no length check in `scripts/check-skill*.mjs` or `packages/spec/scripts/build-skill-docs.ts`. The siblings are not one band either: data 448, ui 447, api 605, ask 829. Keeping 477 is fine.
- **Changeset sentence by sentence.** All three clauses hold against the diff: the description no longer claims the MCP shape and names ask; case 3 is the server-code aggregation; ask gains the metadata-over-MCP negative.

**Landing:** Tier H (`skills/**`). After the C1 one-line docs fix, I delta-read that row, then the seat's contract read follows.

Read at 2026-11-21T11:27Z: card #35859 (body and all four comments), PR 35877 (body, both commits, the net diff against `main`), L1 records 7045169982 and 7061786817, records 7028002670 and 7040518746, the 51 check-runs on this head and the steps of `Type Check · source gates`, the round summary and the `s1-head-to-head` records the card cites, and at this head: the frontmatter of the query, ask, data, ui, api and mcp-build `SKILL.md`, every MCP mention under `skills/objectstack-query/`, the body of ask's `SKILL.md`, the trigger files of query, ask, data and mcp-build, both mirrors, `packages/spec/scripts/build-skill-docs.ts`, the two ratchet rows and `packages/skills/package.json`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Check-runs on the head.** 51 completed: 34 `success`, 17 `skipped`, none red or pending. `Type Check · source gates` is green, and inside it the steps "Check skill docs are generated from SKILL.md frontmatter" and "Published skills token ratchet (#10473) + its self-test" both read `success`. Also green: both `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, both `PR-body guards`, `Build Docs`, `Check Documentation Links`. `mergeable_state` is clean.
- **Surface.** Six files, 18 added, 8 deleted. Under `skills/**`: the `description:` scalar of query's `SKILL.md` (no body line), one prompt in query's trigger file, one added case in ask's. No package source, no schema, no ratchet row, no generator. `main` is past the merge base `9d0772309f`; since then it moved query's `rules/filters.md`, one query eval file, data's body, one ask eval file and the ratchet script. None of the six files here moved, nor either mirror, nor the two ratchet rows (query 5547, ask 1877).
- **Query, ask and data, read as one boundary.** Three request kinds, each with one owner and no overlap:
  - Writing a query in code. Query claims it ("writing a query in app code or a hook"). Ask gives it away by name ("writing a query in application code (see objectstack-query)"), and so does data ("querying records (objectstack-query)").
  - A question answered from the app's records. Ask claims it ("EVERY question answered from the app's records"). Query now gives it away in ask's own words and names ask; mcp-build already did. Query's remaining use-when names code and pagination only, so the claim the card is about is gone, not reworded.
  - A metadata change asked over MCP. Ask gives it away ("building or changing metadata"), query gives it away ("adding objects or fields (objectstack-data)"), data claims it "in a project or through MCP", and mcp-build claims the order of work at the draft door.
- **Query's description against its own bundle.** The body teaches no MCP tool. Its one MCP line, `rules/aggregation.md` line 5, already sends a question asked over MCP to ask. The description now agrees with it.
- **The four names in "Not for"** are directories under `skills/` at this head, and each pointer meets the owner's own description. api's points "request-side query syntax" back at query.
- **Trigger cases against the descriptions.**
  - Query 3 (load): an aggregation "in our ObjectStack app's server code". It meets the use-when ("a query in app code") and the lead ("aggregate by group"), and it is still the bundle's only aggregation positive.
  - Query 3 and ask 1 no longer share a prompt (N1 of record 7040518746). Ask 1 keeps the MCP question as an ask positive. Query 3 and ask 5 are now a matched pair: an ObjectQL aggregation written in code, load for query, leave alone for ask.
  - Ask 7 (leave alone): a field added over MCP. That is ask's first "Do not use" clause, and the same shape is data positives 1 and 2 and mcp-build positive 1. It answers N3 of record 7040518746.
  - Query 1, 2, 4 and 5 (load) and 6 and 7 (leave alone) still meet the lead sentence, the pagination arm and the data and ui exclusions. Case 4 is N3 below.
  - Shape: both files parse; ids run 1 to 7 with no repeat; every case carries `id`, `prompt`, `should_trigger`, `files`. Query has 5 load and 2 leave alone, ask 4 and 3.
- **Generated mirrors.** The folded description is 477 code points and splits at "Use when". Its lead sentence is the `skills/README.md` index cell and the reference table cell. The remainder is the second paragraph of the Query card in `content/docs/ai/skills-reference.mdx`, word for word. `skills/README.md` is the same blob as on `main`, which is right: the generator writes only the lead sentence there, and that did not move. No other file at this head carries either sentence. `packages/mcp/src/ask-skill.generated.ts` comes from ask's `SKILL.md`, which is unchanged.
- **Token ratchet.** Query's `SKILL.md` is 18404 bytes on `main` and 18448 here. Less the 20-byte stamp line that is 4596 and 4607 tokens, against a ceiling of 5547. Ask's is 7520 bytes on both sides, 1875 of 1877. `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` is not in the diff, so no row is raised.
- **Security.** No changed hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication behaviour. The hunks are one routing description and two eval prompts.
- **PR body.** `Fixes #35859`, then exactly one line-initial `Clause-②: no` and one `Metadata-protocol: none`, both bare. No `Skills-docs:` line is owed: that line is owed by a kind other than `none` or by a `(narrowing)` arm. The body's figures (435 and 477 characters, the byte and token readings, 18 added and 8 deleted) match this head.

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/skills': patch` is right. The package ships the `skills/**` tree. This changes one description string and one eval prompt and adds one eval case; it adds or removes no file, export, schema or authorable key. `Clause-②: no` is right (no accept set or public surface widens or narrows). `Metadata-protocol: none` is right (nothing a metadata author can write changes), and `none` takes `patch`. The changeset body carries both lines, bare and line-initial, and each of its two sentences is true of the diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The card's Done-when is met.** The description no longer claims the MCP business question and names objectstack-ask. Case 3 no longer expects query on that question. The ratchet holds with no ceiling raise, and `check:skill-docs` is in sync. `Fixes` is the right keyword.
- **The evidence is the round the card cites, not a new one.** `s1-head-to-head/` holds 12 turns with both bundles installed: ask was launched in 12, query was launched or read in 0, on the branch's bundles and on 18.6.0's alike. No trigger round ran on the new text, so this PASS is on the text against the bundles, not on a trigger rate. The re-measure is #35858. The order L1 asked for holds: this lands before it, or with it.
- **Reword, not flip.** The card allows either. Rewording keeps "aggregate by group" under a positive case, which a flip would not. Accepted. What it leaves without a case is N2.
- **Description length (the dev's flag).** N1.
- **A docs row outside the claim's file surface.** `content/docs/getting-started/build-with-claude-code.mdx` line 419 was ordered by L1 (C1 of 7045169982) and delta-read in 7061786817. It is a prose face and is not reviewed here. It agrees with the new description.
- **Landing tier.** `check-governed-merges --pr 35877`, read before this record: Tier H, three paths on the `skills/**` row. The low-risk skills arm also read Tier H, for want of a record on this head. This record lands nothing by itself.
- **SQL push-down.** No code in the diff.
- **Author.** The PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

- **`skills/objectstack-query/SKILL.md` holds.** I tried to break it three ways.
  - A request left without an owner. The only arm removed is "shaping a records query or aggregation sent over MCP". The body never taught it, ask's own sections 3 and 4 carry the `query_dataset` and `aggregate_records` procedure, and in the head-to-head query was never opened on that request even while its description claimed it. Nothing is orphaned.
  - A request two bundles both claim. None: see ①.
  - An exclusion wider than the owner's claim. It is written in ask's own claim words ("answered from the app's records"), so it is exactly as wide as ask's claim.
- **`skills/objectstack-query/evals/triggers.json` holds.** The new case 3 asks the same data question as before and moves it to where the description claims it. The bundle still has both kinds of case.
- **`skills/objectstack-ask/evals/triggers.json` holds.** Case 7 is the near miss that shares ask's MCP wording, and it covers the "Do not use" clause the two older negatives did not.

**N1 (nit) — the description is 477 characters, and the card's Ask 1 says to pay "in place inside the description length".** The top of the #34769 band is 450, so this is 27 over. No gate reads the length, the token ceiling has 940 of headroom, and no routing depends on it. Accepted deviation. A text inside the band would have to drop the kinds list ("a number, ranking or governed metric"), which holds the words the card's Ask names. If the seat wants the band, do it with the #35858 re-measure, where a trigger round can read the result.

**N2 (nit) — the new exclusion has no case on query's side.** Query's two negatives are data's and ui's ground. The business question over MCP is measured only as ask positives. The dev's reason for not flipping case 3 stands: one bundle per turn cannot show query yielding to ask. But a one-bundle negative still reads whether query leaves that question alone, and on the 18.6.0 text it did not (it read `rules/aggregation.md`). Add one with #35858, for example ask case 2's prompt as a query case that expects no load.

**N3 (nit) — query case 4 names neither ObjectQL nor a code site.** "Search … records by keyword … and return each article's author name" can be read as a list to be answered from the records, which ask also claims ("or a list"). It still meets query's lead sentence (full-text search, expand related records), so the expectation is right with one bundle installed. Cases 1 and 5 say "ObjectQL" and are clear of it. With both bundles installed it is the query positive most likely to go to ask. If #35858 shows that, reword it the way case 3 was.

**N4 (nit) — "an API endpoint (objectstack-api)" lost its verb.** The body treats a query written inside an endpoint as query's ground, and api's description sends "request-side query syntax" back to query. "Not for … an API endpoint" can be read as excluding that; "designing an API endpoint" could not. Restore the verb at the next touch that has room.

**N5 (nit) — three pointers outside this diff are one step short.**
- Data's "Not for querying records (objectstack-query)" sends a business question to query, which now passes it on to ask. There is no gap, only one extra hop.
- Ask's "Do not use for building or changing metadata (the domain skills cover that)" does not name objectstack-mcp-build, which claims exactly the request in ask case 7. The PR body likewise calls that request objectstack-data's. The fixture is right either way: it says only that ask stays unloaded.
- The hand-written "Cross-skill routing" in `skills/README.md` has no bullet for answering a question against writing a query.

Follow-up for each, at the next touch of its file. None changes a reading at this head.
